newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen sluggish at start after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen sluggish at start after jobs data.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open softer on Friday, after the release of data which showed an above-forecast rise in nonfarm payrolls as well as a decline in the unemployment rate.
But stocks might still close higher, as the market digests the day's economic data, some analysts said.

The Labor Department reported that nonfarm payrolls grew by 316,000 in July, up from a revised gain of 228,000 in June. The unemployment rate dipped to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent. But average hourly wages remained steady, allaying some inflation worries, analysts said.

"We might open sluggish to slightly lower, but I would not be surprised to see the market close higher," Sam Stovall, an analyst at Standard & Poor's Industry Reports said. "People might start saying the payroll numbers are quirky because of recent strikes and start discounting them."
Stocks and bonds also face the July National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. It was forecast to read 56.1 compared with 55.7 in June.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off lows but down 1.45 points at 956.65. The long bond was down 11/32 at a 6.33 percent yield.
